final_message:
I reproduced the bug at 4f08332 (eslint 9.14.0, @eslint/config-array 0.18.0). A file on another drive gets linted, while a file on the same drive outside the cwd is ignored as expected.

This VM runs Linux, so the script fakes Windows: Node's `path` module is swapped for `path.win32` and the working directory is set to `C:\Project`. It then lints three paths with `Linter#verify` and with `ESLint#isPathIgnored`/`lintText`:

| File | Result |
|---|---|
| `C:\Project\foo.js` (inside cwd) | linted (correct) |
| `C:\Other\foo.js` (same drive, outside) | "No matching configuration found" / "File ignored because outside of base path" (correct) |
| `F:\foo.js` (different drive) | `isPathIgnored=false`, and `no-undef: 'foo' is not defined` is reported (**the bug**) |

The script exits with code 1 while the bug is present.

**Likely cause:** `ConfigArray#getConfigWithStatus` in `node_modules/@eslint/config-array/dist/cjs/index.cjs` (around line 953) only treats a file as outside the base path when `path.relative(basePath, filePath).startsWith("..")`. On Windows, `path.win32.relative("C:\\Project", "F:\\foo.js")` doesn't produce a `..` path; it returns `"F:\\foo.js"` unchanged. So the file isn't treated as outside, and its ignore patterns are then matched against an absolute path. The same `..` check appears in `shouldIgnorePath` and `isDirectoryIgnored`. The script prints both `path.win32.relative` results so you can see the difference.

I didn't run it on real Windows or through the CLI's `lintFiles`, because that path reads the real file system and can't be faked on Linux.

The script is `repro/cross-drive-ignore.js`. Run it from the repo root after `npm install --ignore-scripts`:

```
node repro/cross-drive-ignore.js
```
